clue.text: Regiment not for light guard duties?

blocks.note: black is the opposite of light
a watch is a spell of guard duty

explanation.surface: A regiment that only stands guard after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Watch is a famous Scottish regiment of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names a specific historic Highland infantry unit, so it is an example of a regiment.

clue.text: Belt buckle worn by men in formal wear

definitions.text: worn by men in formal wear
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the noun

blocks.note: to belt someone is to hit them, as is to cuff them
to buckle is to fasten or join, as is to link

explanation.surface: A belt buckle that a man in evening dress might wear.
explanation.walkthrough: Belt and buckle look like nouns for an item of clothing, but both are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: A cufflink fastens a shirt's double cuff and is typically worn with a dinner suit or other formal dress.

clue.text: Have ambitions for a high place in the church?

blocks.note: taken as written
a spire is the tall pointed top of a church tower

explanation.surface: A cleric hoping for promotion to high office in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High place in the church' suggests a bishopric, but it is a literal high point of the building.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to hope or strive towards some goal, the verb for having ambitions.

clue.text: Very low perch

blocks.note: first meaning: deep in pitch, as of a voice or note
second meaning: a spiny-finned freshwater fish

explanation.walkthrough: 'Very low perch' reads as a bird's seat near the ground; perch is the fish, and the bass is a related species.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes the lowest musical register and also names a perch-like fish.

clue.text: Express delivery-man?

blocks.note: surface reading: a courier who brings parcels quickly
setter's reading: a cricketer whose deliveries of the ball are very quick

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a delivery is one ball sent down by the bowler, so an express deliverer is a pace bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer who bowls at high pace sends down speedy deliveries, hence an express deliverer.

clue.text: Completely out of port and unable to explain why?

blocks.note: first meaning: a ship far out on the ocean, away from harbour
second meaning: confused and bewildered

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the idiom: a sailor wholly offshore and someone baffled share the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom literally means a vessel on the open ocean and figuratively means utterly confused or lost.

clue.text: Affected a stylish greeting

blocks.note: chic means elegant and fashionable
hi is an informal hello

explanation.surface: Someone putting on airs with a fashionable hello.
explanation.definitionFit: Chichi describes something pretentiously showy or precious, which is to say affected in style.

clue.text: Girl in a Fair Isle jumper

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following words, spanning a word break

blocks.note: found across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A girl wearing a patterned Shetland knitted sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair Isle is a Shetland island famous for its patterned knitwear; a jumper is a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is a female given name, so it can stand for a girl in crosswords.

clue.text: Crude oil in a USA state

indicators.note: crude means rough and unrefined, so the letters that follow are in a raw jumbled order

blocks.note: all the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Crude oil drilled in one of the oil-producing American states.
explanation.walkthrough: Crude looks like part of 'crude oil', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisiana is one of the fifty constituent states of the United States, on the Gulf coast.

clue.text: Hard-hearted king whose widow was merry

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for the composer

indicators.note: hearted means having something at the core, so one piece goes into the middle of the other

blocks.note: King Lear of Shakespeare's tragedy
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A cruel monarch whose bereaved wife was cheerful about his death.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz Lehár composed the operetta The Merry Widow; the widow belongs to him only as his work.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hungarian composer Franz Lehár wrote The Merry Widow, so the widow who was merry is his creation.

clue.text: Dead men's chests

blocks.note: surface reading: the pirates' treasure chest of 'Fifteen men on the dead man's chest'
setter's reading: boxes in which the dead are buried

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase recalls the pirate song from Treasure Island; chest here means a box, and a dead person's box is for burial.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffins are the wooden boxes, or chests, in which corpses are laid for burial.

clue.text: Rest can come from these hypnotic states

indicators.note: something that comes from these words is formed out of them in a new arrangement

blocks.note: all the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Hypnotic states can give the mind some rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A trance is a half-conscious condition such as hypnosis induces, so trances are hypnotic states.

clue.text: Leading chess player

blocks.note: surface reading: a top grandmaster
setter's reading: the side that always makes the first move

explanation.walkthrough: Leading means going first, not being the best: in chess the light pieces always open the game.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the player with the light-coloured pieces moves first, so that side leads off every game.

clue.text: Misery of a golf side that's been knocked out

indicators.note: something knocked out of shape has its parts jumbled out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written
all the letters of these words

explanation.surface: The gloom of a golf team eliminated from a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a wretched, unhappy existence, so it stands for misery.

clue.text: Too proud to take lodgers, honest!

blocks.note: to be above doing something is to think it beneath you
to board people is to provide them with lodging and meals

explanation.surface: A landlady too grand to let rooms, and frank about it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes dealings that are open and legitimate, with nothing hidden, so it means honest.

clue.text: Business initiative

blocks.note: first meaning: a company or commercial undertaking
second meaning: boldness and readiness to undertake new projects

explanation.walkthrough: 'Business initiative' reads as one phrase; split it into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a commercial firm and the quality of resourceful drive in starting things.

clue.text: Hobson's choice

blocks.note: surface reading: a choice made by someone named Hobson
setter's reading: the proverbial offer with no real alternative

explanation.walkthrough: Hobson was a Cambridge stable keeper who made customers take the horse nearest the door or none at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobson's choice is an offer with only one option, accept what is given or have nothing, exactly this phrase.

clue.text: Cite ways to develop arctic wilderness

indicators.note: to develop is to grow into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: all the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Suggesting methods to open up the frozen polar regions for development.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen barren expanse, as in polar regions, is a wilderness of the arctic kind.

clue.text: Hairstyle bill rises with the cutting

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading the word from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: a note is a banknote, or bill in American usage
to crop is to cut short

explanation.surface: The barber's charge goes up along with the haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: An Eton crop is a short, slicked 1920s women's haircut named after the boys' school.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eton crop was a fashionable short bobbed haircut for women in the 1920s, so it is a hairstyle.

clue.text: Hirsute one going for a comb

definitions.text: Hirsute one going for a comb

blocks.clueFragment: Hirsute one going for a comb
blocks.note: surface reading: a hairy person reaching for a hair comb

blocks.clueFragment: Hirsute one going for a comb
blocks.note: setter's reading: a furry animal raiding a honeycomb

explanation.walkthrough: The comb is the wax cells of a beehive; the hairy one is an animal with a sweet tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: The honey bear, a name for the sloth bear or sun bear, is a shaggy animal that raids bees' nests.

clue.text: Always brave? Not likely!

blocks.note: first meaning: never afraid
second meaning: a British exclamation of refusal

explanation.walkthrough: As an exclamation the phrase is informal British for 'certainly not!'
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the phrase means absence of fright; colloquially it is an emphatic refusal, like 'no way'.

clue.text: Love to be surrounded by unusually rich voices

indicators.note: being surrounded means sitting inside another group of letters
unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters are in an odd order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A lover enveloped by remarkably rich singing.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is a body of singers, a collective of voices performing together.

clue.text: Uncertain opportunity

definitions.note: adjective: chance in the sense 'accidental, unpredictable'

blocks.note: first meaning: happening by luck
second meaning: an opening to do something

explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncertain opportunity' reads as one phrase, but it is two meanings side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an unpredictable, accidental occurrence and a favourable opening to act.

clue.text: North America's largest meat producer

blocks.note: surface reading: a giant meatpacking company
setter's reading: the biggest land animal on the continent, hunted for meat

explanation.walkthrough: Producer suggests a company; it is the animal itself, the bison, North America's heaviest land mammal.
explanation.definitionFit: The American bison, commonly called buffalo, is the continent's heaviest land animal and was hunted for meat.

clue.text: Child born before Lincoln

indicators.note: before places one piece ahead of the next in the answer

blocks.note: b is the abbreviation for born in dates and genealogy
Abe is the nickname of President Abraham Lincoln

explanation.surface: An infant born in the days before the president.
explanation.definitionFit: A babe is a baby or very young child, an old-fashioned word for an infant.

clue.text: It became obsolete when the market backed the automobile

definitions.text: It became obsolete when the market backed the automobile

indicators.note: backed means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse order

blocks.note: a mart is a market
a car is an automobile

explanation.surface: A vehicle made redundant when buyers chose motor cars instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is history as well as wordplay: street trams were scrapped as cars took over.
explanation.definitionFit: Street tramcars disappeared from many cities once private motor cars and buses won public favour.

clue.text: A picking-up point

blocks.note: surface reading: a collection place, like a bus stop
setter's reading: a pointed prong used for spearing and lifting food

explanation.walkthrough: Point means a sharp tip, not a place: each prong of a fork lifts food.
explanation.definitionFit: A tine is one prong of a fork, a sharp point used to pick things up.

clue.text: An explosive expletive

blocks.note: first meaning: a detonation
second meaning: a curse word

explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive expletive' sounds like a furious oath; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a violent detonation and a mild oath uttered in annoyance.

clue.text: Rush over to meet

blocks.note: first meaning: dash from one side to the other
second meaning: encounter by chance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush over to meet' reads as hurrying to greet someone; it is two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to sprint to the far side and to come upon someone unexpectedly.
